senses.d: The absolute height of a location, usually measured from sea level.
ex: As the altitude increases, the temperature gets lower, so remember to bring warm clothes to the mountains.

senses.d: A vertical distance.

ex: All three altitudes of any triangle will always meet at point known as the orthocentre or orthocenter.

senses.d: The length of such a line; the distance measured perpendicularly from a figure's vertex to the side opposite to the vertex.
ex: The perpendicular height of a triangle is known as its altitude.

senses.d: The angular distance of a heavenly body above our Earth's horizon.
Height of rank or excellence; superiority.
Elevation of spirits; heroics; haughty airs.

senses.d: Highest point or degree.

senses.d: Happening by turns; one following the other in succession of time or place; first one and then the other (repeatedly).
ex: And bid alternate passions fall and rise
The service is half-hourly as far as Harrogate and Knaresborough, with alternate trains going on to York.

senses.d: Alternating; (of e.g. a pair of tinctures which a charge is coloured) succeeding in turns, or (relative to the field) counterchanged.
ex: Goldschmidt (Austria; creation July 27, 1862): [...] party, argent and gules, an eagle of alternate colors, [...]

senses.d: Designating the members in a series, which regularly intervene between the members of another series, as the odd or even numbers of the numerals; every other; every second.
ex: the alternate members 1, 3, 5, 7, etc.

senses.d: Other; alternative.
ex: Hyperlinked text is displayed in alternate color in a Web browser.
He lives in an alternate universe and an alternate reality.

senses.d: Distributed singly at different heights of the stem, and at equal intervals as respects angular divergence
ex: Many trees have alternate leaf arrangement (e.g. birch, oak and mulberry).

senses.d: That which alternates with something else; vicissitude.
ex: Grateful alternates of substantial peace.

senses.d: A substitute; an alternative; one designated to take the place of another, if necessary, in performing some duty.
ex: An alternate for the first-string quarterback played the entire first half.
Corridors beyond this point have collapsed. I'm looking for an alternate. Careful.

senses.d: A proportion derived from another proportion by interchanging the means.
A replacement of equal or greater value or function.
To perform by turns, or in succession; to cause to succeed by turns; to interchange regularly.
ex: The most high God, in all things appertaining unto this life, for sundry wise ends alternates the disposition of good and evil.

senses.d: To happen, succeed, or act by turns; to follow reciprocally in place or time; followed by with.
ex: The flood and ebb tides alternate with each other.

senses.d: To vary by turns.
ex: The land alternates between rocky hills and sandy plains.
